chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Abu Ismail al-Sarraj Abdullah ibn Uthman, from Qudama ibn Abi Yazid al-Hammar, from some of our companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), he said:

I asked him: 'What is the minimum distance that should be between the well — the water well — and the cesspool?' So he said: 'If the ground is flat (plain), then seven cubits; and if it is rocky (mountainous), then five cubits.'

Then he said: 'The water flows toward the qibla direction, to the right; and flows from the right side of the qibla toward the left side of the qibla; and flows from the left side of the qibla toward the right side of the qibla; and cannot flow from the qibla direction toward the opposite direction (behind the qibla).'

key_terms.أذرع: Cubits (plural of dhira'/cubit), an ancient unit of measurement approximately 45-50cm
key_terms.البئر: Water well, used for drinking and ritual purposes
key_terms.القبلة: The qibla, the direction of prayer toward the Kaaba in Mecca
key_terms.جبل: Rocky/mountainous ground, hard impermeable rock that limits contamination spread
key_terms.سهل: Flat/plain ground, soft permeable soil where contamination spreads more easily

ai.seo_question: What is the minimum distance between a well and a cesspool according to Imam Sadiq in al-Kafi?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) provides a legal ruling on the minimum required distance between a water well and a cesspool (sewage drain) to prevent contamination: seven cubits on flat land and five cubits on rocky ground. He then explains the permissible directions of water flow relative to the qibla (prayer direction), indicating that lateral flows are acceptable but flow directly away from the qibla is not. This ruling pertains to ritual purity (taharah) — ensuring drinking water remains uncontaminated by nearby sewage — and reflects Islamic jurisprudence's concern with both physical cleanliness and practical engineering principles of that era.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Muhammad Bin Ismail, from Abu Ismail Al Sarraj Abdullah Bin Usman, from Qudamat Bin Abu Yazeed Al Hammar, from one of our companions, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, said, ‘I asked him<sup>asws</sup>, ‘How close by can there happen to be between the water well and the cesspool (drain of dirty water)?’
So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘If it was a plain then seven cubits, and if it was a mountain, so five cubits’.

Then he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The water flows to the direction to the right, and flows from the right direction to the left direction, and flows from the left direction towards the right direction, and cannot flow from the direction to the opposite direction’.
en.sarwar: 3. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Muhammad ibn ’Isma‘il from abu ’Isma‘il from al-Sarraj from ‘Abd Allah ibn ‘Uthman from Qudamah ibn abu Yazid al-Hammar from certain persons of our people who have said the following: “I once asked abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about the distance needed between a well and a cesspool.
He (the Imam) replied, ‘If the ground is plain, the distance must be seven yards; and if it is a hillside the distance must be five yards.’
He (the Imam) then said, ‘Water flows forward in direction, to the right or to the left or from its left side to its right side (in) forward direction but it does not flow backward.’”
